chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUbayd Allah al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, he said:
When you stand in the last two rakʿahs, do not recite in them; rather say: al-ḥamdu lillāh, subḥāna Allāh, and Allāhu akbar.
He only forbade him from reciting while believing that anything other than recitation is not permissible, not from reciting it by way of choice and seeking merit.

And it is possible that his statement, 'Do not recite in them,' is informative, not prohibitive; as though he said: If you are not among those who recite, then say: al-ḥamdu lillāh, subḥāna Allāh, and Allāhu akbar.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ: the final two units of salat (prayer)
key_terms.الِاخْتِيَارِ: personal choice in selecting a permissible form
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ: praise belongs to Allah; a prescribed dhikr here
key_terms.الْقِرَاءَةِ: the recitation, meaning Qur'anic recitation in salat (prayer)
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: glory be to Allah; a form of dhikr recited in the final two rakʿahs
key_terms.طَلَبِ الْفَضْلِ: seeking additional merit or virtue through an optional act
key_terms.لَا تَقْرَأْ: do not recite; possibly phrased as information rather than prohibition in context

ai.seo_question: In the last two rakʿahs of salat (prayer), should one recite or say tasbih?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for the final two rakʿahs of salat (prayer), indicating the permissibility of tasbih in place of recitation. It clarifies that any prohibition concerns believing recitation to be exclusively required, while reciting instead of tasbih remains allowed by choice and in seeking extra merit.
